traditions.name: Stoicism
traditions.note: Western Hellenistic philosophy; included for comparison, not classified as Eastern.

traditions.name: Buddhist traditions
traditions.note: Branches are kept distinct; no single Buddhist school is treated as representative of all Buddhism.

traditions.name: Hindu / Indian philosophical traditions
traditions.note: Vedanta, Yoga, Samkhya, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, and Mimamsa remain distinct schools even when a sourcebook covers several.

traditions.name: Daoist traditions
traditions.note: Classical texts and later religious Daoism are related but not identical.

traditions.name: Confucian traditions
traditions.note: Confucian self-cultivation is not reduced to generic productivity or self-help.

traditions.name: Jain traditions
traditions.note: Core themes include nonviolence, non-attachment, and many-sidedness; sectarian distinctions remain explicit.

traditions.name: Japanese philosophical and religious traditions
traditions.note: Zen and Pure Land are represented in the Buddhist hierarchy; these branches cover additional Japanese traditions.

traditions.name: Sikh philosophy and theology
traditions.note: Included as a distinct South Asian tradition rather than folded into Hindu or generic Eastern philosophy.

traditions.name: Epicureanism
traditions.note: Western Hellenistic philosophy included for comparative reading.
